issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer reaches into root logger handlers to find OTLP LoggingHandler — leaky abstraction across module boundary
issues.detail: The contract of init_recording / _setup_cloud_tracer should be: 'after I run, OTLP logging is wired up.' Instead, _flush_early_log_buffer performs reflection on the root logger to discover the OTLP LoggingHandler instance that _setup_cloud_tracer just installed. This violates the module boundary — JobContext now depends on an implementation detail of telemetry.traces (that the OTLP handler is registered on the root logger as a LoggingHandler instance). If _setup_cloud_tracer ever attaches the handler elsewhere (e.g., to a specific logger, via a LogRecordProcessor, or wraps it), this silently breaks. The fix is to give traces.py an explicit replay/emit API (e.g., _replay_records(records)) that owns the knowledge of where the OTLP handler lives.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler exposes mutable internal buffer as public attribute — leaky ADT
issues.detail: The _BufferingHandler ADT promises 'buffer records for later replay,' but its only state — self.buffer — is a public mutable list with no encapsulation. Callers in job.py iterate handler.buffer directly. The invariant 'records are only appended in emit order, never mutated externally' is not enforced. A proper ADT would expose drain() or replay(target_handler) and hide the list. This also entangles two responsibilities: buffering AND knowing how to replay through an external handler. Either give the handler a replay(other) method (so the boundary stays inside traces.py), or make buffer a read-only snapshot.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry mutates root logger handlers as a side effect — undocumented postcondition
issues.detail: _shutdown_telemetry's stated contract is 'shut down telemetry providers.' The new implementation also removes every LoggingHandler instance from the root logger before flushing. This is a postcondition change that is not reflected in the function name or any docstring: after this call, the root logger's handler set has been altered. Any caller that installed its own LoggingHandler-derived handler (the type check is by class, not identity) will silently lose it. State the new postcondition explicitly in a docstring and narrow the removal to handlers this module owns (e.g., track them in a module-level registry when installed).

issues.description: init_recording overloaded with two contracts: 'configure recording' and 'cleanup buffering' — SPEC-MISSING
issues.detail: init_recording now has a branching contract: in the early-return path (already initialized OR not cloud), it now ALSO stops log buffering as a side effect. The function's name and signature promise one thing (initialize recording) but it performs an unrelated cleanup. A caller reading the signature cannot know that calling init_recording when not is_cloud(url) will dismantle a buffering handler. This is exactly the kind of hidden coupling that makes long-lived systems fragile. Either split into init_recording() and a separate _finalize_log_buffering() called from both paths, or document the postcondition prominently.

issues.description: _on_cleanup silently swallows init_recording failure with bare except Exception
issues.detail: The new crash-path in _on_cleanup catches Exception broadly and only logs. This is reasonable defensively, but the invariant 'after _on_cleanup returns, _early_log_handler has been removed from the root logger' is only preserved because _stop_log_buffering is called in the except branch. If init_recording raises after partially mutating state (e.g., setting _recording_initialized = True before _flush_early_log_buffer runs), the handler may remain attached. State the cleanup invariant explicitly and ensure _stop_log_buffering runs in a finally, not just on exception.

issues.description: Unbounded buffer in _BufferingHandler — missing invariant on capacity
issues.detail: The _BufferingHandler ADT has no stated invariant on buffer size. If a crash takes a long time to surface (e.g., a hung connect with verbose logging), this buffer grows without bound while attached to the root logger. The contract should specify a maximum capacity with a drop-oldest or drop-newest policy, so the abstraction's resource behavior is part of its promise rather than incidental to the implementation.

issues.description: _on_entry_done conflates two responsibilities: error logging and shutdown triggering
issues.detail: The renamed callback now both logs the exception AND forces _shutdown_fut to resolve. These are distinct concerns; combining them makes the trigger-shutdown-on-crash behavior invisible at the call site (add_done_callback). Consider splitting into two callbacks, or at minimum renaming to something like _on_entry_done_trigger_shutdown that signals the second responsibility. The contract on _shutdown_fut also subtly changes: previously it was only set by orderly shutdown paths; now it can be set by a crash callback, so any downstream code reading shutdown_info.reason must handle 'job crashed' as a new variant.

review.summary: The PR solves a real problem — crash logs were being lost — and the buffer-then-replay design is sound at the algorithmic level. From an abstract-data-type lens, however, the implementation crosses module boundaries that should remain sealed: JobContext reaches into the root logger to find the OTLP LoggingHandler that telemetry.traces installed, and _shutdown_telemetry now silently mutates the root logger's handler set as an undocumented postcondition. The _BufferingHandler ADT exposes its internal buffer as a public mutable attribute and has no capacity invariant, mixing 'buffer' and 'replay through external handler' responsibilities. init_recording has been overloaded to also stop log buffering in its early-return path, hiding cleanup behind a name that promises only initialization. The contracts of _shutdown_fut and _on_entry_done have shifted in ways that callers cannot see from the signatures. Recommended: give telemetry.traces an explicit replay API that owns OTLP-handler knowledge, encapsulate _BufferingHandler.buffer with a drain/replay method and capacity bound, document the new postconditions on _shutdown_telemetry and _shutdown_fut, and split the buffering-cleanup concern out of init_recording.
